subject: Packages Rstudio server and Shiny server

messages.author: 5c02fb642297ea7d
messages.subject: Packages Rstudio server and Shiny server
parts:
What are best practices for managing packages for a Shiny server and an Rstudio server, that reside on the same machine?

I currently have one Centos VM that is both an RStudio server and a Shiny server.  I ramping it up to be a resource for my group.  Is anyone doing the same thing?  Are you leaving the packages up to each individual "R developer" to install and manage?  Or does it makes sense to configure both servers to look at the same set of libraries and have a centralized package management process?  Based on the what we'll be using it for I am leaning towards the latter.

That being said, how do you set this Linux box up so that there is only one list of packages that both Rstudio and Shiny use?

Thanks for any suggestions.

Brent

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Packages Rstudio server and Shiny server
parts:
If you set up Shiny Server as autouser/user_apps (see the configuration overview) then RStudio Server and Shiny Server will automatically share the same package library for each user. So each user can install packages using RStudio Server and they will be available to their own Shiny apps. This is how we run glimmer.rstudio.com.

You as the superuser can also install libraries in the system-wide R library, which will again be available to both RStudio and Shiny. To do this, run "sudo su - R" and install whatever packages you want from that R prompt, and they should be installed in the system-wide library.
